correctness.rationale: The zero-run invariant follows by induction from W_(m+1)=W_m 0^((q-2)q^m) W_m. The first phrase family has a reproduced longest proper prefix starting at 1, but any earlier full occurrence would require (q-2)L+1 zeros following an earlier one; no such earlier one exists. The second family has an earlier all-zero proper prefix in the long gap, but a full earlier occurrence would require a longer preceding zero run than any prior one has. Phrase end/start indices telescope exactly. Exceptional q=3 initial six phrases are checked symbol-by-symbol before the same infinite families apply. At lengths q^k, counting starts proves the two linear-in-k formulas; the included independent program checks both morphic constructions and full start lists for q=3..12.

originality.rationale: The primary 2006/2007 source defines precisely this exhaustive history and proves Θ(log n) for exponentially growing nonperiodic morphic words; its relevant definitions, main theorems, examples, and final comparisons were inspected and no explicit generalized Cantor phrase boundaries occur. MFCS 2006 Berstel–Savelli studies Crochemore parsing, which does not imply equality of exhaustive phrase starts. Targeted searches of the published mathematical research database returned no statement covering either the two-phase Cantor boundaries or the exceptional q=3 boundaries, and accessible prior mathematical-claim ledgers concern different invariants. The full Crochemore text was inaccessible, leaving a residual but not decisive comparison risk.

value.rationale: This is the complete infinite exhaustive parsing of an established natural uniform morphic family, with two precise recurring phrase phases and a genuine exceptional ternary base. The integer breakpoint classification and exact finite-stage 2k+constant count are not consequences of the published broad Θ(log n) classification. The recurrence provides an explicit fine-grained relation between compression histories and sparse Cantor positional geometry. The theorem does not claim a new compression algorithm or large quantitative improvement.
